signals.label: Rejected at the gate
signals.rule: The House rejected the nomination after a vetting hearing.
signals.why: Rejections are the rare documented cases where committee scrutiny changed an outcome. Their stated grounds are primary evidence.

signals.label: Returned after dissolution
signals.rule: Approved in the 2024 reconstitution after holding a cabinet seat (CS, Prime CS or Attorney General) in the cabinet dissolved on 11 Jul 2024.
signals.why: A protest-forced dissolution that returns many of the same people is only visible when appointment histories are linked per person.

signals.label: Docket rotation
signals.rule: Held two or more different cabinet-level portfolios across the record.
signals.why: Rotation moves the same officials between ministries; the audit trail of each docket should follow the person.

signals.label: Soft landing
signals.rule: Left a cabinet office by dissolution, dismissal or removal, then was nominated to a different public office such as an envoy post.
signals.why: Removal is often a lateral move. When a removed official re-enters public office, the earlier record should resurface with them.

signals.label: Committee overruled
signals.rule: The vetting committee recommended rejection; the House approved the nominee anyway.
signals.why: When the only committee rejection in a cycle is overturned on the floor, the gate is shown to be advisory. The override belongs in the record.

signals.label: Gazetted without approval
signals.rule: The appointment was published in the Kenya Gazette although the nominee never appeared and the House never approved it.
signals.why: The vetting gate only closes on nominees who walk through it. A no-show reaching the Gazette, even in error, is a control failure worth tracking.

signals.label: Declined nomination
signals.rule: The nominee publicly declined the nomination.
signals.why: Declines are part of the exit pathway and are rarely recorded alongside outcomes.

signals.label: Elevated without a hearing
signals.rule: Assumed the office of Deputy President without a committee vetting hearing equivalent to a CS nomination.
signals.why: Lawful under Art. 149, but it is a gap between the rigour applied to appointments and the rigour applied to elevations.
